currentContext.expansion: The Company's principal expansion project of recent years - the new integrated world-class manufacturing platform at Toopran, near Hyderabad - is complete and fully operational. Production has been successfully transitioned to the site, and the Chairman notes the platform is meeting global industry benchmarks within a short span of two years. The plant is designed to enhance capital efficiency, improve product quality and optimise costs, and was built around sustainability and Industry 4.0 principles, emphasising resource conservation, data-driven intelligence, ergonomic design for safety, water sustainability and effective use of renewable energy. Distribution 'capacity' is being expanded through digital transformation rather than bricks - management describes fortifying the distribution network to deepen reach in core markets and increase penetration in emerging geographies, supported by 850+ wholesale dealers and 10 lakh+ retail outlets served from seven regional offices. No new plant, line or capex project with a future commissioning date or a capex rupee value is disclosed in the sections provided.

risks.risk: Regulatory restrictions on tobacco could impair long-term revenue growth
risks.note: The Company operates under an increasingly stringent regulatory regime (COTPA guidelines on packaging and labelling, advertising and promotion), complicated by differing regimes across states and lack of consensus on interpretation. Restrictive rules subject to interpretation could result in penalties or loss of reputation, and could impair the ability to communicate with adult smokers or to meet consumer expectations through new brand launches or geographic expansion. Mitigation is continuous social dialogue with stakeholders and the regulatory community through industry bodies, plus building capability to launch compliant, consumer-acceptable brands.

Manufacturing and marketing of cigarettes accounts for 100% of the business activity reported in the BRSR, with cigarettes containing tobacco at 84.8% of turnover and unmanufactured tobacco at 15.2%. There are no subsidiaries or joint ventures to diversify the earnings base, so any category-level shock (tax, regulation, consumption) transmits directly.

risks.risk: Water scarcity across the sourcing base
risks.note: BRSR material issue: tobacco cultivation is water-intensive, exposing the business and its supply chain to water scarcity risk; any disruption in water availability directly affects raw material supply. Mitigated through water management and harvesting initiatives across sourcing geographies, Zero Liquid Discharge operation at the Toopran unit, periodic monitoring of withdrawal/consumption/discharge, a formal Water Stewardship Policy, a water risk assessment, and AWS Gold certification for Toopran.

BRSR material issue flagged with negative financial implications: GHG emissions are central to the Company's climate response and tightening carbon policy frameworks across operating regions create growing regulatory exposure. Mitigation is annual measurement and tracking, progressively increasing renewable energy use, transitioning to cleaner fuels, and working with the agricultural supply chain to reduce Scope 3 emissions.

BRSR material issue with negative financial implications: energy management reduces operating cost and mitigates supply-scarcity risk, and supports compliance with evolving statutory requirements. Mitigation is facility-level consumption tracking and a structured energy management strategy that progressively increases the renewable share of the energy mix.

BRSR material issue: farmers face significant challenges around sustainable agricultural practices that can affect the quality and availability of the Company's raw material; a stable sourcing base depends on farmers thriving. The Company is strengthening farm productivity initiatives focused on soil quality, seed quality and mechanisation of field operations.

risks.risk: Leaf tobacco export demand and price realisation cycle
risks.note: Higher crop production across Brazil, Zimbabwe, Malawi and India increased global leaf availability and pushed international prices down; importers optimised inventory and staggered buying, slowing procurement and extending shipment timelines, so the Indian industry faced subdued demand amid intensified competition among exporting countries. Order and shipment movement was slow during the year.

risks.risk: Employee attrition in a small workforce
risks.note: Permanent employee turnover was 23% in FY 2025-26 (30% for females) after 34% in FY 2024-25, against a total headcount of 712 people as at 31st March 2026 comprising 359 management staff and 353 workmen - a structural retention exposure for an organisation this size, only partly addressed through campus hiring, Development Centres, leadership IDPs and internal promotion.

risks.risk: Waste management, particularly tobacco product waste
risks.note: BRSR material issue with negative financial implications: management of tobacco product waste is material to environmental performance. Hazardous waste from manufacturing is disposed of exclusively through PCB-approved recycling vendors, with generation monitored to stay within regulatory permissible limits.

risks.risk: Health and safety of the workforce
risks.note: BRSR material issue: strong H&S performance is directly linked to the ability to attract and retain quality talent and to standing as a responsible employer. Health and safety practices are deployed in line with established H&S policies, with ongoing monitoring including hazard identification and risk assessments across the value chain.

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: A more than 90-year-old Indian cigarette manufacturer and leaf-tobacco business, an associate undertaking of British American Tobacco Plc, operating an integrated world-class plant at Toopran and a nationwide distribution network.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: VST Industries manufactures and markets cigarettes in India, serving adult consumers through a portfolio that mixes heritage trademarks with newer, insight-led offerings, and also runs a leaf tobacco business that procures from Indian farmers and supplies domestic and export customers. Production is anchored at a single integrated manufacturing platform at Toopran near Hyderabad, supported by regional offices at Hyderabad, Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, Guwahati and Lucknow, and leaf operations at Guntur. The Company describes its portfolio in two buckets - New Age Brands, which address evolving consumer preferences, and Growth Heritage Brands, which address established demand segments.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Cigarettes - New Age Brands:** TOTAL, EDITIONS
- **Cigarettes - Growth Heritage Brands:** CHARMS, SPECIAL, MOMENTS
- **Leaf tobacco:** Unmanufactured tobacco

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Adult smokers across diverse socio-economic segments in India
- Domestic market presence spanning 26 States and 6 Union Territories
- Wholesale and retail trade - 850+ wholesale dealers and 10 lakh+ retail outlets
- Export markets for leaf tobacco, where India competes with origins such as Brazil, Zimbabwe and Malawi

certifications.title: Certs (RHP)
certifications.body:
- Gold rating in Water Stewardship Certification from Water Stewardship and Assurance Services (AWS), Scotland - Toopran facility
- NABL certification for the R&D Centre laboratory at Toopran - process of obtaining initiated, not yet obtained

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian cigarette market estimated at about Rs. 1,20,000 Crores in 2025 with a forecast CAGR of about 9.50% over 2026-2034 (source cited as IMARC Group), supported by a large adult consumer base, strong brand loyalty, extensive retail distribution and sustained demand across price points
- Structural supports cited: rising disposable incomes, urbanisation, premiumisation and broad retail reach
- Premiumisation - consumers showing increased interest in higher-quality products, refined blends, differentiated formats and stronger brand experiences, especially in urban and higher-income cohorts
- Value pricing still anchors the category - value-priced cigarettes accounted for more than 51% of the market in 2025; traditional tobacco shops accounted for a substantial part of the market
- Mid-premium is the growth pool - it accounts for over 40% of the industry and strengthened further in FY 2025-26 driven by legacy brands and convenient pricing, while the low-price segment underperformed
- Industry volume grew about 7% in FY 2025-26 on a stable regulatory and taxation regime for most of the year; the Company grew about 9%, ahead of industry, after four consecutive years of volume decline
- FY 2026-27 is expected to be a complex year defined by a big change in the taxation structure; management calls the tax increase on cigarettes unprecedented in known history and says its effects could last well beyond FY 2026-27
- Headwinds flagged for the year ahead: supply chain and margin pressures, intense price competition in all segments, heightened price sensitivity among consumers and the threat/potential expansion of illicit trade
- Leaf tobacco - a soft global market on higher crop production across Brazil, Zimbabwe, Malawi and India put downward pressure on international prices; importers optimised inventory and staggered buying, slowing procurement and shipments
- Management remains cautiously optimistic on the medium-term outlook for the global tobacco market, expecting India to retain its position as a reliable supplier of quality tobacco as global inventories normalise and demand stabilises
- Competitive advantage is expected to rest less on market momentum and more on sharper portfolio architecture, pricing discipline, efficient supply chains, strong retail reach, differentiated brand propositions and compliance-ready operations
- Leaf tobacco: the pace of order and shipment movements remained relatively slow during the year, with extended shipment timelines as global importers adopted cautious, staggered procurement

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Portfolio calibration - sharpen brand architecture across value, mainstream and mid-premium offerings, supporting resilient franchises while using targeted innovation to address evolving adult consumer preferences
- Build the mid-premium franchise, a segment that accounts for over 40% of the industry, on the back of TOTAL as a pan-India youth-centric brand and EDITIONS as the second pan-India brand and a multi-format mid-premium/premium proposition
- Continue investing in heritage trademarks Charms, Special and Moments to defend leadership in the value segment in their respective regions
- Segmented, insight-led innovation - newer launches such as Editions Trio, Total Spin and Total Paan Delight
- Execution excellence - translate strategy into action through pricing discipline, market responsiveness, sharper channel execution and tighter operating control
- Operational strength as a strategic lever - run the fully operational integrated Toopran platform with stronger process discipline, supplier oversight and logistics resilience for both efficiency and future readiness
- Digital enablement - continue the digital transformation to fortify the distribution network, deepen reach in core markets and increase penetration in emerging geographies
- Cost agility and compliance discipline across the business
- Continue to invest in product innovation, re-engineering of heritage constructs, new formats and better alignment with adult consumer preferences
- Strengthen the leaf sourcing ecosystem through agronomic support, disciplined procurement, customer relationships and digital procurement and traceability systems
- The Company reports on a standalone basis and states that it has no subsidiary, associate or joint-venture companies, so capital is deployed entirely within the listed entity. Cash return to shareholders is the primary use: the Board recommended a final dividend of Rs. 12 per equity share for the year ended 31st March 2026 for Members' approval at the 95th AGM. Governance around deployment is conservative - prior approval of the Audit Committee is obtained for all related-party transactions, the Nomination and Remuneration Committee has formulated a Board-approved policy for directors', KMP and employee remuneration, and a Whistle Blower Policy provides a vigil mechanism with direct access to the Chairman of the Audit Committee. Board oversight is exercised through an Audit Committee constituted under Regulation 18 of the SEBI Listing Regulations and Section 177 of the Companies Act, whose remit covers the financial reporting process and auditor appointment, and the Members are being asked to appoint M/s. Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP as Statutory Auditors for five consecutive years from the 95th AGM to the 100th AGM in 2031. As on 31st March 2026 the Board comprised eight Directors, of which four are Independent Directors, and an annual Board evaluation covering the Board, its committees and individual directors was completed with the Directors expressing satisfaction with the process.
- Toopran manufacturing unit operates on a Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) basis and holds AWS (Alliance for Water Stewardship) Gold certification from Water Stewardship and Assurance Services, Scotland
- Formalised Water Stewardship Policy plus a completed water risk assessment; specific water consumption reduced by 5% year on year through best practices for sustainable development
- 1.2 MW photovoltaic solar plant commissioned in September 2022 currently fulfils approximately 33% of the Company's electricity needs and has enabled a 37% reduction in its carbon footprint; performance improved 3% over FY 2024-25
- Progressive clean-energy build-out: 10 KW solar lighting system in 2024 upgraded to 15 KW in 2025, and EV charging stations for two- and four-wheelers at the Toopran facilities
- Replaced High-Speed Diesel with Piped Natural Gas as primary incinerator fuel, expected to cut carbon emissions by an estimated 51% and save approximately Rs. 189 Lakhs of fuel cost annually; boiler and incinerator fuel efficiency improved 4.5% over FY 2024-25
- Energy conservation: 15% energy saved in utilities (DRF, Airwash, Compressor) and production operations, 1.2% saved in lighting via LED and solar fittings, with an energy conservation awareness programme run for 268 employees
- Developing a structured energy management strategy that progressively increases the share of renewables in the energy mix, with facility-level energy consumption tracking
- Annual measurement and tracking of GHG emissions, progressive increase in renewable energy use and transition to cleaner fuels, and engagement with the agricultural supply chain to reduce Scope 3 emissions through sustainable farming practices
- Responsible leaf tobacco sourcing framework integrating sustainability across agronomy, procurement and supplier engagement - prioritising soil and water stewardship, deforestation prevention, safe agrochemical use, elimination of child labour and improved farmer livelihoods, embedded in contracts and SOPs, reinforced through field technicians and monitored via inspections and digital traceability systems
- Sustainable supply chain framework developed, with sustainability criteria being progressively extended across all sourcing categories; non-leaf suppliers assessed against quality, delivery and price standards
- Farm productivity programme focused on soil quality, seed quality and mechanisation of field operations to raise farmer earnings and secure the sourcing base
- Hazardous waste from manufacturing units disposed of exclusively through PCB-approved recycling vendors, with generation monitored to remain within regulatory permissible limits
- EHS training completed by 375 employees and 102 contract workmen during the year, with mock drills and half-yearly and annual EHS audits of operations
- Internal Complaints Committee established under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, with no cases reported during the year; grievance redressal mechanisms in place for all stakeholder groups with no complaints filed or pending
- Recognised with the Best Management Award for 2025 by the Telangana Government for progressive people practices and strong management systems

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company's principal expansion project of recent years - the new integrated world-class manufacturing platform at Toopran, near Hyderabad - is complete and fully operational. Production has been successfully transitioned to the site, and the Chairman notes the platform is meeting global industry benchmarks within a short span of two years. The plant is designed to enhance capital efficiency, improve product quality and optimise costs, and was built around sustainability and Industry 4.0 principles, emphasising resource conservation, data-driven intelligence, ergonomic design for safety, water sustainability and effective use of renewable energy. During the year the Company institutionalised TQM (Total Quality Management) and 5S workplace-discipline projects at the plant. Beyond the core plant, capability additions are incremental rather than greenfield: the R&D Centre's Laboratory Management Systems have been implemented at the new Toopran factory location and the process of obtaining NABL certification for the relocated laboratory has been initiated. On renewable capacity, a 1.2 MW photovoltaic solar power plant was commissioned in September 2022 and now meets approximately 33% of the Company's electricity needs, supplemented by a 10 KW solar lighting system installed in 2024 and an upgraded 15 KW solar lighting system in 2025, plus electric-vehicle charging stations for two- and four-wheelers at the Toopran facilities. Distribution 'capacity' is being expanded through digital transformation rather than bricks - management describes fortifying the distribution network to deepen reach in core markets and increase penetration in emerging geographies, supported by 850+ wholesale dealers and 10 lakh+ retail outlets served from seven regional offices. No new plant, line or capex project with a future commissioning date or a capex rupee value is disclosed in the sections provided.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Associate undertaking of British American Tobacco Plc, which anchors technology, governance and manufacturing standards
- Wide and deeply embedded distribution network - 850+ wholesale dealers and over 10 lakh retail outlets, with seven regional offices covering the country
- Two national trademarks - TOTAL and, newly, EDITIONS - alongside heritage trademarks CHARMS, SPECIAL and MOMENTS, giving portfolio coverage across value, mainstream and mid-premium segments
- Single integrated Toopran plant built for capital efficiency, product quality and cost optimisation, with TQM and 5S institutionalised during the year
- In-house R&D Centre developing competitive products that management says are gaining traction with adult consumers
- Data-driven distribution and a comprehensive digital infrastructure ecosystem enabling targeted market activity and portfolio expansion in core, emerging and weak markets
- More than 90 years of continuous presence in the Indian cigarette industry

risks.body:
- Regulatory restrictions on tobacco could impair long-term revenue growth — The Company operates under an increasingly stringent regulatory regime (COTPA guidelines on packaging and labelling, advertising and promotion), complicated by differing regimes across states and lack of consensus on interpretation. Restrictive rules subject to interpretation could result in penalties or loss of reputation, and could impair the ability to communicate with adult smokers or to meet consumer expectations through new brand launches or geographic expansion. Mitigation is continuous social dialogue with stakeholders and the regulatory community through industry bodies, plus building capability to launch compliant, consumer-acceptable brands.
- Single-activity and single-product concentration — Manufacturing and marketing of cigarettes accounts for 100% of the business activity reported in the BRSR, with cigarettes containing tobacco at 84.8% of turnover and unmanufactured tobacco at 15.2%. Mitigated through water management and harvesting initiatives across sourcing geographies, Zero Liquid Discharge operation at the Toopran unit, periodic monitoring of withdrawal/consumption/discharge, a formal Water Stewardship Policy, a water risk assessment, and AWS Gold certification for Toopran.
- Emissions and tightening carbon policy — BRSR material issue flagged with negative financial implications: GHG emissions are central to the Company's climate response and tightening carbon policy frameworks across operating regions create growing regulatory exposure. Mitigation is annual measurement and tracking, progressively increasing renewable energy use, transitioning to cleaner fuels, and working with the agricultural supply chain to reduce Scope 3 emissions.
- Energy cost and supply scarcity — BRSR material issue with negative financial implications: energy management reduces operating cost and mitigates supply-scarcity risk, and supports compliance with evolving statutory requirements. Mitigation is facility-level consumption tracking and a structured energy management strategy that progressively increases the renewable share of the energy mix.
- Farmer livelihood and raw-material quality/availability — BRSR material issue: farmers face significant challenges around sustainable agricultural practices that can affect the quality and availability of the Company's raw material; a stable sourcing base depends on farmers thriving. The Company is strengthening farm productivity initiatives focused on soil quality, seed quality and mechanisation of field operations.
- Leaf tobacco export demand and price realisation cycle — Higher crop production across Brazil, Zimbabwe, Malawi and India increased global leaf availability and pushed international prices down; importers optimised inventory and staggered buying, slowing procurement and extending shipment timelines, so the Indian industry faced subdued demand amid intensified competition among exporting countries. Order and shipment movement was slow during the year.
- Employee attrition in a small workforce — Permanent employee turnover was 23% in FY 2025-26 (30% for females) after 34% in FY 2024-25, against a total headcount of 712 people as at 31st March 2026 comprising 359 management staff and 353 workmen - a structural retention exposure for an organisation this size, only partly addressed through campus hiring, Development Centres, leadership IDPs and internal promotion.
- Waste management, particularly tobacco product waste — BRSR material issue with negative financial implications: management of tobacco product waste is material to environmental performance. Hazardous waste from manufacturing is disposed of exclusively through PCB-approved recycling vendors, with generation monitored to stay within regulatory permissible limits.
- Health and safety of the workforce — BRSR material issue: strong H&S performance is directly linked to the ability to attract and retain quality talent and to standing as a responsible employer. Health and safety practices are deployed in line with established H&S policies, with ongoing monitoring including hazard identification and risk assessments across the value chain.
